subject: mathematics
title: Launch and diagnostic: rational and irrational numbers
essential_question: How can understanding real numbers and irrational numbers help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
learning_objectives: Activate prior knowledge about rational and irrational numbers, surface initial thinking without penalty, and establish the unit question.
Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of rational and irrational numbers.
Check, revise, or improve work about rational and irrational numbers using stated success criteria.
success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about rational and irrational numbers.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Present a brief, accessible prompt connected to “rational and irrational numbers.” Ask the learner to notice, predict, estimate, recall, or pose a question before instruction.

Model the idea concretely or visually, represent it symbolically, compare strategies, and require an explanation of reasoning. Keep the explanation centered on rational and irrational numbers. Name the success criteria and model how to check work or evidence.
Complete two supported examples or source-based tasks about rational and irrational numbers. After each step, ask: “What evidence or reasoning supports that move?” Fade prompts on the second example.
Learner completes a new application of rational and irrational numbers and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about rational and irrational numbers; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.

student_activity: Learner completes a new application of rational and irrational numbers and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
formative_check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about rational and irrational numbers; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence/reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid approaches when they meet the criteria. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for rational and irrational numbers, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.
Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for rational and irrational numbers works before continuing.
Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of rational and irrational numbers, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review.
Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking rational and irrational numbers mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Use worked examples, explanation, error analysis, application, and a second occasion of evidence; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions when feasible.
extension: Apply rational and irrational numbers under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting rational and irrational numbers.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

learning_objectives: Build a clear mental model of selecting linear or nonlinear models through an explicit worked example, demonstration, text, or phenomenon.
Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of selecting linear or nonlinear models.
Check, revise, or improve work about selecting linear or nonlinear models using stated success criteria.
success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about selecting linear or nonlinear models.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Present a brief, accessible prompt connected to “selecting linear or nonlinear models.” Ask the learner to notice, predict, estimate, recall, or pose a question before instruction.

Model the idea concretely or visually, represent it symbolically, compare strategies, and require an explanation of reasoning. Keep the explanation centered on selecting linear or nonlinear models. Name the success criteria and model how to check work or evidence.

Complete two supported examples or source-based tasks about selecting linear or nonlinear models. After each step, ask: “What evidence or reasoning supports that move?” Fade prompts on the second example.
Learner completes a new application of selecting linear or nonlinear models and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about selecting linear or nonlinear models; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.

student_activity: Learner completes a new application of selecting linear or nonlinear models and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
formative_check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about selecting linear or nonlinear models; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence/reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid approaches when they meet the criteria. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for selecting linear or nonlinear models, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.
Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for selecting linear or nonlinear models works before continuing.
Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of selecting linear or nonlinear models, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review.
Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking selecting linear or nonlinear models mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Use worked examples, explanation, error analysis, application, and a second occasion of evidence; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions when feasible.
extension: Apply selecting linear or nonlinear models under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
